inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E net sales. H1-2026 actual 7,555 + H2-2025 actual 2,654 = 10,209 trailing, plus the New Corteva commercial agreements (+169 pro forma FY2025, ~+130 for H2) and ~1-2% underlying H2 growth. Cross-check: pro forma FY2025 10,067 x 1.03 = 10,369; Analysis JSON cites ~10.4bn expected for FY2026. FY0 is an estimate because the valuation date is three-quarters through the fiscal year and H1 (planting season) is ~75% of annual sales, so FY2026 is largely known.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 667.018m issued at 30-Jun-2026 (1:1 with Corteva, Form 10 pro forma) + 1.2m dilutive awards (pro forma H1-2026 diluted 671.6 vs basic 670.4 weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.net_debt_note: YEAR-END NORMALISED, not the 30-Jun seasonal peak and not the carve-out allocation figures. Pro forma 30-Jun-2026 (Form 10): cash 1,100; short-term borrowings 3,179; long-term debt 2,480; total 5,659 -> June net debt 4,559. 30-June is the working-capital peak (H1 OCF -2,471; H2-2025 OCF was +4,063 as receivables collect and ~3.2bn of December prepayments arrive), so the short-term borrowings unwind by December. Management targets 0.8-1.1x debt / operating EBITDA at YE2026; on ~2.8bn operating EBITDA (27% of ~10.4bn) that is 2.25-3.1bn gross, midpoint ~2,660 = the durable 2,480 of long-term notes plus ~180 of residual short-term/CP. Cash held at the pro forma 1,100 (December cash is normally higher because of prepayments; no credit taken). Net debt = 2,660 - 1,100 = 1,560 (~0.56x operating EBITDA, ~0.65x clean EBITDA). H2-2026 one-off cash obligations and the unfunded pension are charged separately in equity_bridge. Carve-out balance-sheet debt (5 / 15 / 112) and cash (630 / 599 / 836) are Corteva allocations and are NOT used.
inputs.fcf_basis: 3-year average FY2023-FY2025 (mid-cycle), not a single year. Reported FCF 429 / 1,439 / 2,160 (avg 1,343); SBC 31 / 35 / 43 (avg 36); interest income 87 / 42 / 50 (avg 60); owner FCF 311 / 1,362 / 2,067 (avg 1,247). FY2025 was flattered by ~+470 of working capital (deferred revenue 2,902 -> 3,232 at December) and carried no Bayer cash outflow (the 610 charge was accrued in FY2025 and ~546 paid in H1-2026); FY2023 was depressed by ~-780 of working capital. `sbc` (43) is the latest actual, the anchor for sbc_pct_path (0.43% of sales; 0.5% assumed standalone). Equity-award taxes 0 in all years (carve-out).
inputs.mid_cycle_note: Component build for FY2026E: 10,350 x 23.0% clean EBITDA = 2,380; - SBC 52; - D&A 807 = EBIT 1,521; cash tax 24% = 365; NOPAT 1,156; + D&A 807 - capex 352 - WC 30 = ~1,550 (15.0% of sales). This is pre-interest (unlevered); the ~175/yr pro forma interest belongs to the debt deducted in the bridge, not the flows. It sits between the 3-year owner-FCF average (1,247, dragged by FY2023 working capital) and FY2025 (2,067, flattered by working capital), and is ~1,300 ex-working-capital-swings history plus the net-royalty tailwind.
inputs.sbc_source: Combined Statements of Cash Flows, VYLR_Annual_FY2025.txt (share-based compensation add-back 43 / 35 / 31; equity statement shows 42 / 34 / 30). No equity-award tax line in the carve-out; EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in the carve-out statements (parent-level Corteva buybacks reduced the 1:1 share basis 709 -> 667 over FY2023-H1-2026, but that cash was Corteva's). Flat count is a modelling convention Vylor has not yet paid for; management's stated return is a dividend of ~15% of CFO from Q4 2026, not buybacks.
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026 is an estimate (FY2026E): H1-2026 actual is in the combined statements, H2 is estimated from H2-2025 plus the commercial agreements. Y1 = FY2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:02:53Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); listed 1-Oct-2026 so the 52-week range is seven sessions of history
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.1% (10y UST, Oct-2026); beta 0.9 (Corteva's 2-year beta 0.8-0.9 as a proxy -- Vylor has seven trading days of its own history); ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (new Vylor notes 2.3-5.625%, weighted ~4.2-4.7%; pro forma interest 175 on ~3.9bn average debt), ~3.4% after tax; debt ~6% of EV at target leverage -> WACC ~8.3%, rounded UP to 8.5% for the untested standalone credit and the absence of a trading record. Same 8.5% in all three scenarios: cyclicality, farm-income cycle and standalone execution are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost (~90/yr) is inside opex and therefore already inside EBITDA (treatment B); operating lease liabilities of 297 at 31-Dec-2025 are EXCLUDED from net debt. No finance leases. No lease_cost_pct_path needed because the cost is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Pro forma NCI is 6 (equity) and ~1-2/yr of profit -- immaterial; flows treated as fully attributable, no bridge deduction.
inputs.pension_treatment: Unfunded US defined-benefit and OPEB liability 226 at 31-Dec-2025 (BS line 'Pension and other post-employment benefits'); deducted after tax (~170) in equity_bridge as a debt-like item. Service cost is already in EBITDA; non-operating pension cost (~11/yr) is in other income and excluded from the clean margin.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical row of the routing table; adaptations file read for cyclical/working-capital/lease/NCI rules). First valuation of this ticker -- no memory entry. VALUES VYLOR ALONE: a former CTVA holder's combined claim is VYLR + New Corteva (CTVA ~US$13.24, Crop Protection only). HISTORY IS SHORT: Seed carve-out combined statements FY2023-FY2025 + H1-2025/H1-2026 only; the Corteva consolidated pages in the information statement are NOT Vylor. EBITDA BASIS: the model's margin is CLEAN EBITDA pre-SBC = statutory EBITDA + significant items (Bayer 610, separation costs, restructuring) + SBC - interest income: FY2023 ~1,822 (19.2%), FY2024 ~1,992 (20.9%), FY2025 ~2,299 (23.2%); trailing H1-2026 + H2-2025 ~23.8%. It is BELOW management's 'operating EBITDA' (FY2026 ~27%, FY2029 3.3-3.7bn) because that basis also excludes FX/exchange losses, losses on receivable sales, non-operating pension and allocated corporate items (~100-400/yr of real cash cost), and the SegmentOperatingEBITDA kpi (3,413 FY2025) excludes a further ~1bn of unallocated costs -- neither is a cash-flow basis. Management's Investor Day targets are the BULL anchor, not the base. FY2025 EARNINGS ARE NOT RUN-RATE: statutory NI 574 includes the 610 Bayer resolution charge (other income (expense) -712) and 35 of separation costs; pro forma FY2025 NI 324 also carries 201 of separation costs and the new 175 of interest. The Bayer settlement ended Roundup Ready royalties to Bayer (net royalty cost 439 in FY2025 vs 317 gross out-licensing income; management targets royalty neutrality in 2026) -- that tailwind is what carries the base margin from 23% to 25.5%. STANDALONE COSTS: ~175/yr interest is below EV (in net debt), dis-synergies and the standalone board/plans are in the 23.0% FY2026E margin (vs 23.8% trailing) and the 0.5% SBC. D&A (8% of sales) far exceeds capex (3.4%) because of DowDuPont-merger intangible amortisation; the gap is kept (non-cash, not replaced) and the cash tax rate on post-amortisation EBIT is 24-25% (cash taxes paid 118 / 155 / 235 vs GAAP ETR 30-32%, with royalty non-deductibility falling away). WORKING CAPITAL: a seed producer carries inventory and grower receivables against large December prepayments; 3-year net working-capital flow was about -170 on ~+430 of revenue growth, so wc_capture is negative (growth consumes cash). PRICE: the current quote is a regular close; the stock is seven sessions old, so expect volatility as the CTVA index/flowback churn settles.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored: FY2029 net sales 11.2-11.9bn vs ~10.4bn FY2026 implies 2.5-4.6%/yr; base takes 3.0% (low end), bull 4.5% (upper-mid), bear a farm-cycle dip then 2%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Only two years of growth history (FY2023-FY2025 Seed carve-out); 3- and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed. Revenue 2-yr CAGR 2.2% (9,472 -> 9,898). Net income 652 -> 574 (-4.2%/yr) is distorted by the FY2025 Bayer charge; ex-Bayer after tax ~1,030 gives +24.8%/yr, which is an FY2025 clean-up, not a trend. Owner FCF 311 -> 2,067 is working-capital noise, not growth. Shareholders' equity is parent net investment in a carve-out (14,324 -> 13,234 after distributions to Corteva) and carries no growth information. Clean EBITDA 1,822 -> 2,299 (+12.3%/yr) is the one series with signal, and it is mostly margin (royalty, mix), not volume. Selected rate therefore comes from guidance, not history.
historical_growth.notes: No pre-2023 Seed-only statements and no VYLR price history before 1-Oct-2026: historical-multiple checks have seven trading days to work with. SBC (0.3-0.4% of sales) is immaterial to the CAGR comparison.

base.narrative: Growth at the low end of the FY2029 guidance band (FY2029 sales ~11,310 vs 11.2-11.9bn guided); clean EBITDA margin from 23.0% FY2026E to 25.5% by FY2032 as net royalty goes from -439 to neutral/positive and out-licensing scales, i.e. roughly two-thirds of the way to management's 27%->30% operating-EBITDA expansion on a cash basis. D&A drifts from 7.8% to 7.0% as merger intangibles roll off; capex 3.4% (FY2025 actual); cash tax 24-25% on post-amortisation EBIT. Terminal 16x owner FCF (cap binds; Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would be 17.1x) ~10.5x terminal clean EBITDA.

bull.narrative: Management's Investor Day delivered: FY2029 sales ~11,810 (upper-mid of 11.2-11.9bn), clean margin to 28.5% (their 30% operating-EBITDA target less ~1.5pp of FX/receivable-sale/pension costs that basis excludes). Triple-stack corn out-licensing from 2027, MDR gene-edited corn 2028, Brazil soybean share gains and hybrid wheat all land; working capital less consumptive as prepayment programs grow with the licensing mix. Terminal growth 3.0% for the IP-royalty stream.

bear.narrative: The farm-income downturn bites in FY2027 (sales -3%, a 2015-16-style grower cutback, corn acres shifting to soy) and FY2028 is flat; the royalty tailwind is competed away through pricing as Bayer/BASF/Syngenta respond and standalone dis-synergies are not fully offset, so clean margin settles at 21.5% (below the FY2025 actual). Growth platforms slip (hybrid wheat, MDR corn) and are not in the numbers; capex higher at 3.6% for standalone IT/production. Terminal growth 2.0%; Gordon (15.7x) binds below the 16x cap.

scenario_narratives.base: Vylor alone -- the Seed business, not the pre-spin Corteva; a former CTVA holder's combined claim is VYLR plus New Corteva (CTVA ~US$13.24). Base: a 3%-a-year grower off a FY2026E base of ~10.35bn (low end of the FY2029 11.2-11.9bn guidance), with clean EBITDA margin expanding from 23% to 25.5% as the January-2026 Bayer settlement ends Roundup Ready royalty outflows and the out-licensing business moves from a 439 net cost toward neutrality and beyond. Owner FCF ~1,550 in FY2026E (15% of sales) rising toward ~2,300 by FY2036 before capitalising at 16x. The axes are: the farm-income cycle (grower seed spend), execution on the royalty flywheel, and whether standalone dis-synergies offset the royalty gain.
scenario_narratives.bull: Investor Day targets delivered on a cash basis: 4.5% growth to FY2029 (~11.8bn), clean margin 28.5% by FY2031 (operating EBITDA ~30%), out-licensing becomes a net income line early, gene-edited MDR corn launches 2028 and hybrid wheat begins to scale -- the business re-rates as an IP platform rather than a seed seller. Even here value is well below the current quote, which is the finding: at ~31x FY2026E owner FCF for a 3-4% grower the market is already paying for the bull case and then some.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026-27 US farm-income trough (net cash receipts down ~18bn, corn/soy/wheat below 10-year averages) cuts seed demand and pricing just as Vylor absorbs standalone costs and new interest; competitive response erodes the royalty tailwind; the new growth platforms slip. Sales dip 3% then stall, clean margin settles ~21.5%. No solvency issue -- net debt is ~0.7x EBITDA even in this path -- so the bear is a multiple-and-margin case, not a survival case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the stock lists into a documented farm-income downturn, carries new leverage and interest, has no standalone operating or credit record, and the FY2025 clean run-rate is itself an estimate on a 610 one-off. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the bull needs several independent things to go right (royalty flywheel, MDR corn regulatory/commercial launch, hybrid wheat adoption, Brazil share) across a 10-year window, and management's targets are on an operating-EBITDA basis that excludes real cash costs. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Vylor on the cash it can hand to owners after SBC, standalone interest (via net debt), separation one-offs and the seasonal working-capital cycle -- not on management's operating EBITDA, which excludes ~100-400/yr of real cash costs and whose segment variant excludes ~1bn. The earnings base is a mid-cycle component build (FY2026E owner FCF ~1,550, between the 3-year average of 1,247 and the working-capital-flattered FY2025 print of 2,067), net debt is normalised to a December basis rather than the June seasonal peak, and management's FY2029 targets anchor the bull case only. This values Vylor alone; a former Corteva holder's claim is VYLR plus New Corteva (CTVA ~US$13.24).
key_risks_to_valuation: Earnings base: only three years of Seed-only history, all inside Corteva; the clean FY2025 EBITDA (~2,300) rests on adding back a 610 Bayer charge and separation costs, and the FY2026E margin is an estimate with H2 still to report

Net debt basis: year-end normalisation assumes the ~3.2bn of June short-term borrowings unwind in H2 as in prior years; a weak collection season or a change in prepayment behaviour would leave net debt nearer 2.5-3bn than 1.6bn (~-$1.5-2/share)
Margin ramp: the 23% -> 25.5% base path is the net-royalty tailwind; if competitive pricing absorbs it the base collapses toward the bear margin
Farm-income cycle: FY2026-27 grower economics are the weakest in a decade; the bear's -3% is a mild version of 2015-16
D&A/tax: cash tax is modelled on post-amortisation EBIT at 24-25%; if merger-intangible amortisation is not tax-deductible the cash rate could run higher (~28%), ~-$2/share
Terminal: 16x owner FCF cap binds in base and bull; the market is paying ~31x FY2026E owner FCF, so the gap to price is mostly a terminal-multiple disagreement, not a flow disagreement
Post-spin flowback and index churn: seven sessions of trading; CTVA holders' combined claim (VYLR + CTVA) is the reference, not VYLR alone
